cards.text: David is king over Israel now (2 Samuel 5:3), and he gathers the chosen men of Israel again, thirty thousand in all. THIRTY THOUSAND. Friend, I run a whole bakery by myself and some mornings I can't round up one oven mitt.

cards.question: David and his thirty thousand set out for Baale of Judah. What are they going to bring up from there?

cards.text: And this is no ordinary chest. The ark is called by the Name, the name of the LORD of Hosts, who is enthroned between the cherubim on it.
They set the ark on a new cart and bring it from the house of Abinadab, up on the hill. Abinadab's sons, Uzzah and Ahio, are guiding the cart.

cards.question: Uzzah and Ahio are guiding the new cart with the ark on it. True or false: Uzzah is the one walking in front of the ark.
As the cart rolls along, what are David and all the house of Israel doing before the LORD?

answers.text: Celebrating with all kinds of instruments
Following behind it in total silence

cards.text: Harps, tambourines, sistrums, cymbals, the WORKS, and Mags, my little bell, would've rung the whole way. Then at the threshing floor of Nacon, the oxen stumble.

cards.question: The oxen stumble at the threshing floor of Nacon. Uzzah reaches out and takes hold of the ___.

cards.text: Hold on. The anger of the LORD burns against Uzzah.

cards.question: The anger of the LORD burns against Uzzah. What happens to him?

answers.text: God strikes him down on the spot
God sends him away from Israel

cards.question: Uzzah took hold of the holy ark of God, and God struck him down on the spot for his ___.
Uzzah dies right there beside the ark of God. True or false: David becomes angry because the LORD burst forth against Uzzah.

cards.text: Back at Baal-perazim, David said the LORD burst out against his enemies (2 Samuel 5:20). Now the LORD has burst forth against Uzzah, and David names this place Perez-uzzah, as it's called to this day.
That same day David fears the LORD, and he asks, “How can the ark of the LORD ever come to me?” I bet that question kept him up all night.

cards.question: After asking how the ark could ever come to him, David moves it into the City of David anyway. True or false?

cards.text: Instead, he takes it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. So Obed-edom just got a brand new houseguest, and it's the ark of God.

cards.question: The ark of the LORD stays at Obed-edom's house for three months. What happens to Obed-edom and his household?

answers.text: The LORD blesses him and his household
Nothing changes for them at all

cards.text: Then King David gets a report: the LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of God. Friend, that's the houseguest EVERYBODY wants now.

cards.question: David hears the LORD has blessed Obed-edom's house because of the ark. What does David do?

answers.text: Brings the ark up into the City of David
Leaves the ark with Obed-edom for good
Sends the ark back to Abinadab's house

cards.question: Last time, the ark rode on a new cart. True or false: on this trip, it rides on a cart again.

cards.text: This time people carry the ark, and when they've gone six paces, David sacrifices an ox and a fattened calf.

cards.question: As the ark comes up, David is wearing a linen ephod. What does he do before the LORD?

answers.text: Kneels the whole way in silence

cards.text: David dances with ALL his might while he and all Israel bring up the ark with shouting and the ram's horn. I'd join in, but on this gold base my best move is a hop. One hop. That's the whole routine.

cards.question: As the ark enters the City of David, Saul's daughter Michal looks down from a window and sees King David leaping and dancing before the LORD. How does she feel about him in her heart?

cards.text: They set the ark of the LORD in its place inside the tent David pitched for it. Then David offers burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

cards.question: When the burnt offerings and peace offerings are finished, David ___ the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts.

cards.text: Then David hands every man and woman in the crowd a loaf of bread, a date cake and a raisin cake, and everybody heads home. Personally I'd have gone with cookies, but nobody asked the stamper.

cards.question: David goes home to bless his own household, and Michal comes out to meet him. True or false: she greets him by sincerely praising how he honored the LORD today.

cards.text: “How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today!” she says, and friend, that is NOT a compliment. I can hear that tone from here, and I live on a cookie planet.

cards.question: What does Michal say David did today in the sight of the maidservants?

answers.text: Uncovered himself like a vulgar person
Forgot to bless his own household

cards.question: David answers Saul's daughter: he was dancing before the LORD, who chose him over her ___ and all his ___ to rule the LORD's people Israel.
So after Michal's words, what does David say about his celebrating before the LORD?

answers.text: He'll celebrate and humble himself even more
He'll only dance in private from now on
He'll let the priests do the celebrating

cards.text: He even says he'll be honored by the very maidservants Michal brought up. Some people dance like nobody's watching, but David dances before the LORD, and he is NOT stopping.
And the passage closes on this: Michal the daughter of Saul had no children to the day of her death.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: "David dances with ALL his might while he and all Israel bring up the ark with shouting and the ram's horn." / "I'd join in, but on this gold base my best move is a hop." / "One hop." / "That's the whole routine." Story cards after the opening card can have only 1 to 2 sentences. Fold the joke into fewer sentences or trim it.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The second blank ("all his ___", answer "house") asks the baker to guess David's exact wording from 6:21, which they haven't seen. Nothing in the earlier cards lets them reason toward "house" over "army" or "servants". The setup "David answers Saul's daughter" also makes the first blank, "father", obvious. Rework the card so it tests meaning, for example who the LORD chose David over, instead of the next words of the line.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Whether Uzzah or Ahio walks in front of the ark (6:4) is a minor detail. It doesn't move the passage forward, and the baker doesn't need it to understand the passage. Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason it out, so the pick is a coin flip. The stop already spends a discovery question on card 2. Tell this detail on a story card, or ask about something that matters.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: The question calls it "the holy ark of God". In 2 Samuel 6:6-7 the text calls it "the ark of God" and never "holy". The added word comes from outside the passage with no reference, and it also works as a hint toward "irreverence". Use the text's own name for it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
